edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. II, 3

source_text: Fasciculus stactes — id est guttae sive stillae — fratruelis meus mihi. Guttam, unguem, casiam, galbanum in Exodo legimus praecepto Dei in thymiama compositum. Stacten vero unguentum pretiosum esse noverimus. Fasciculum ergo stactes fratruelem suum dicit, quia totus Christus, totus Dei Sermo, unguentum est et fragrantia. Inter ubera mea commorabitur: in pectore et in principali cordis Christi sensus et memoria requiescat.
pass_a_gloss: Bundle of-stacte — that is of-drop or droplet — my brother to-me. Drop, onycha, cassia, galbanum in Exodus we-read by-command of-God into incense compounded. Stacte however precious ointment we-should-know to-be. Bundle therefore of-stacte her brother she-calls because whole Christ, whole Word of-God, is ointment and fragrance. Between my breasts he-will-linger: in breast and in ruling-part of-heart Christ's sense and memory let-rest.
pass_b_english: [[A bundle of myrrh — that is, of drop or droplet — is my brother to me >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:13]]. We read in Exodus of drop, onycha, cassia, galbanum compounded into incense by God’s command. But let us know that stacte is a precious ointment. She calls her brother a bundle of myrrh, because the whole Christ, the whole Word of God, is ointment and fragrance. [[He shall linger between my breasts >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:13]]: in the breast and in the ruling part of the heart let Christ’s meaning and memory rest.
notes: Song Homilia II OET; Lawson not used for wording.
